sections.advice: Food stop near Crépy-en-Valois → High point near Creil is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.

This High point near Creil → Scenic stretch near Meulan-en-Yvelines stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

Scenic stretch near Meulan-en-Yvelines → Ézy-sur-Eure, on the way back is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

Photo stop near Corbreuse → Pierrefitte-sur-Seine can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

scenicChapters.title: Langar → Khargush Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 156 km. 4344 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall — a steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Khargush Pass → Murghab
scenicChapters.narrative: 257 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

wakhan-corridor-road-yamchun-murghab.story: 522 km from Khandūd to Murghob, about 7 h 10 of riding. On the way it passes Langar and Khargush Pass. The highest point is about 4,500 m. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
